.claude/hooks/agent-idle.sh: This fires whenever an AI helper finishes a tool call or stops working entirely, telling the background process to mark that helper as no longer busy.
.claude/hooks/agent-start.sh: This fires the moment an AI helper is about to spawn, sending a quick signal to the background process so it can start tracking the new helper.
.claude/hooks/agent-stop.sh: This fires when an AI helper finishes its task and tells the background process to clean up or record the result depending on whether the helper was running in the foreground or background.
.claude/hooks/agent-substop.sh: This fires when a background helper finishes its work and tells the background process to close out that specific helper's record.
.claude/hooks/agent-touch.sh: This fires every time an AI helper uses a tool, sending a quick message to the background process so it can update what the helper is currently doing and which file it's touching.
.claude/hooks/description-refresh.sh: After any file is edited, this quietly reminds the active agent of two things: update the file's plain-English description if the edit changed what the file is for, and jot down any non-obvious lesson into the small lessons file.
.claude/hooks/learnings-surface.sh: Before any file is edited, this peeks at any lessons we have already recorded about that file — or the folder it lives in, or general project lessons — and quietly slips them into the agent's view so it does not re-discover what we already wrote down.
.claude/hooks/lib/config.sh: This looks up where Constellation stores its settings and figures out which door to knock on when sending messages — shared by every other hook script.
.claude/hooks/session-start.sh: This fires when a Claude Code session starts or restarts, clearing out leftover state from previous sessions so the visualizer doesn't show stale agent badges.
.claude/scheduled_tasks.lock: This is a small lock record that tracks which running process currently owns scheduled tasks, preventing two processes from stepping on each other.
.claude/settings.json: This is the list of rules that tells Claude Code which hook scripts to run when AI helpers start, stop, use tools, or a session begins — wiring up the live agent display, the file descriptions file, and the lessons file.
.claude/skills/constellation/feedback/SK: This is the instructions for a '/constellation:feedback' shortcut that lets you file a privacy-redacted bug report against Constellation directly from inside Claude Code, with a confirmation step before anything is sent.
.compound-engineering/config.local.examp: This is an example of the optional local settings you can add to customize the Compound Engineering tooling for this project.
.context/compound-engineering/ce-review/: This is a saved report from a reviewer who tried to break the pin feature and found five real bugs — including a hover that gets permanently stuck when the panel closes while your cursor is inside it.

This is a saved review checking whether the new pin feature could be seen or controlled by AI agents — it passes for the live-agent display but flags that pin state is invisible to agents, which is acceptable for now.
This is a saved report hunting for logic errors in the hover and pin features, finding five issues including one where moving the mouse too quickly could make the hover panel vanish unexpectedly.
This is a saved report hunting for timing bugs — situations where two things happen in the wrong order — finding eight issues in the hover, pin, and scroll interactions.
This is a saved report from a strict code-quality reviewer who found seven places where the code makes unsafe assumptions about what kind of thing it is working with.
This is a saved report looking for duplicated logic and misplaced values, finding six places where the code could be simplified or made more consistent.
This is a saved report checking whether the new code follows this project's own conventions — it passed every check.
This is a saved report looking for gaps in how the new features were tested, finding two real bugs and several scenarios that were never exercised.
.gitignore: This is the list of files that the project's history machine should ignore — temporary files, secrets, build output, and runtime state.
app/api/agents/route.ts: This answers the question 'which AI agents are working right now?' — it asks the background process first, and reads saved files from disk as a fallback if the process isn't running.
app/api/agents/stream/route.ts: This keeps a live connection open between the visualizer in your browser and the background process, so agent movements appear on the map within a fraction of a second.
app/dev/zoom-perf/page.tsx: This is a hidden developer test page (not linked from the main map) that puts 5,000 fake tiles on screen to check that zooming and panning stays smooth before rolling out to large real codebases.
app/dev/zoom-perf/ZoomPerfClient.tsx: This is the interactive part of a developer test page that renders 5,000 fake tiles and lets you zoom and drag to measure how well the map holds up on large codebases.
app/globals.css: This sets the visual rules for the whole app — background color, fonts, and the tile highlight colors that appear when you hover a file, pin it, or see its connections.
app/layout.tsx: This is the wrapper that surrounds every page in the app, loading the font and global styles so everything else can count on them being there.
app/page.tsx: This is the home page — it scans the chosen project on the server, then hands the result to the interactive map and the live-agent display in your browser.
bin/constellation: This is what runs when you type 'constellation' in your terminal — it figures out which command you asked for and hands it off to the right piece.
CLAUDE.md: This is the project's living handbook for the AI working in this repo — it explains the architecture, the rules, and everything that must stay accurate as the code changes.
cli/add.mjs: This is what runs when you type 'constellation add' — it wires the current folder into Constellation by copying hook scripts, updating settings, and registering the repo with the background process.
cli/describe.mjs: This is what runs when you type 'constellation describe' — it uses Claude to write a plain-English, one-sentence description for every file in the repo and saves them so the tiles have text to show.
cli/description-tone.txt: This is the instruction sheet Claude reads when writing tile descriptions — the rules about plain language, length, banned words, and style that keep all descriptions consistent.
cli/help.mjs: This prints the list of available commands when you type 'constellation help' or run 'constellation' with no arguments.
cli/list.mjs: This is what runs when you type 'constellation list' — it shows every repo Constellation knows about and whether any AI agents are currently active in them.
cli/logs.mjs: This is what runs when you type 'constellation logs' — it shows the background process's log (or the visualizer website's log with --web), with an option to keep watching live.
cli/open.mjs: This is what runs when you type 'constellation open' — it launches your browser straight to the visualizer, pointed at the repo you're currently in.
cli/rm.mjs: This is what runs when you type 'constellation rm' — it unregisters the current repo from Constellation, with an option to also remove the hook scripts.
cli/service.mjs: This manages starting, stopping, and installing both Constellation pieces — the background process and the visualizer website — as system services that survive reboots (Mac only).
cli/status.mjs: This is what runs when you type 'constellation status' — it shows whether the background process and the visualizer website are running right now, and on Mac whether they're set up to come back automatically after a restart.
cli/util.mjs: This is the shared toolbox for all the CLI commands — helpers for finding the right folder paths, reading settings, and talking to the background process.
components/AgentBubble.tsx: This is the little speech bubble above each agent dot that shows what the agent is currently doing — reading, writing, searching, or something else.
components/AgentIcon.tsx: This is the colored circle that appears on the map when an AI helper is active — sky-blue for the main agent, emerald for foreground helpers, amber for background ones, with an animated ring while they're busy.
components/AgentOverlay.tsx: This puts all the agent dots on top of the map, keeps them anchored to the right file tiles as agents move around, and fades them in and out as they appear and disappear.
components/DetailSlider.tsx: This is the 'Detail' slider in the header that lets you show more or fewer small tiles on the map at once.
components/Glyph.tsx: This draws the tiny shape next to each exported name in the hover card — a circle for a visual element, a diamond for a page route, a square for a hook or type — so you can see what kind of thing it is at a glance.
components/HoverContext.tsx: This is the shared memory that lets the map and all the file tiles agree on which file is hovered or pinned without passing that information through every layer of the tree.
components/HoverPanel.tsx: This is the little card that floats next to your cursor and tells you about whichever file you're pointing at — it stays open when you click to pin, and you can scroll it and select text from it.
components/LodContext.tsx: This remembers how much detail the slider is set to and turns that into a minimum tile size, sharing it with the whole map so tiny tiles can disappear and reappear as you adjust.
components/PinController.tsx: This listens for the Escape key and clicks outside the map to unpin the current tile, and also keeps the hover card anchored to its tile as you zoom and pan.
components/RepoSwitcher.tsx: This is the top-left part of the header that shows which repo you're looking at and lets you arrow between repos that have active Claude sessions.
components/RoadmapToggle.tsx: This is the 'Roadmap' button in the header — clicking it drops down a panel that shows what you're working on right now, what's on deck for the next few days, weeks, and months, and what just shipped, all read straight from the project's roadmap file.
components/SymbolRow.tsx: This draws one line in the hover card's 'Exports' list — a small shape and the name of whatever the file shares with the rest of the project.
components/TileRegistry.tsx: This keeps a running list of every file tile currently on screen so the agent dots and the pinned panel can find and follow a tile's exact position without scanning the whole page.
components/TreemapNode.tsx: This draws one piece of the map — either a folder (which slices its space and draws its children) or a file tile that highlights, fades, and shows its description when the right file is hovered or pinned.
components/Visualizer.tsx: This is the big interactive map you see on the screen — it handles hovering and clicking tiles, scrolling to zoom, dragging to pan, and pressing 'f' to fit everything back in view.
components/ZoomPanContext.tsx: This shares the current zoom and pan state with the parts of the app that need to stay anchored — like agent dots and the pinned panel — without routing live gesture values through React and causing slowdowns.
constellation.config.json: This is the bundled default settings — the ports the background process and visualizer run on, the list of tools to watch, and the agent staleness timeout — copied to your home folder on first run.
daemon/activity.ts: This turns a tool name and its inputs into a short human-readable phrase like 'Reading config.ts' or 'Searching for squarify' — the text that appears in each agent's thought bubble.
daemon/atomic-write.ts: This saves each agent's current state to a file safely, writing to a temporary file first then swapping it in, so readers never see a half-written result.
daemon/disk-sync.ts: This batches rapid save requests so when an agent touches many files quickly, the disk only gets written to once every 50 milliseconds instead of on every single tool call.
daemon/index.ts: This is the startup sequence for the background process — it boots everything, loads leftover state from the last run, starts listening for events, and shuts down cleanly when asked.
daemon/lifecycle.ts: This remembers which AI helpers are currently working in your project and what each one is doing right now — all updates go through a single place so there are no conflicts.
daemon/registry.ts: This is the persistent list of repos Constellation knows about, saved to disk and updated whenever a repo is added, removed, or seen for the first time.
daemon/server.ts: This is the mailbox the rest of the system drops messages into when something happens. It also answers questions like 'who's working right now?' and 'which repos are registered?'
daemon/sse.ts: This pushes live updates to every open browser tab the moment something changes, so when an agent moves to a new file your map updates in under a second.
daemon/transcripts.ts: This watches the log files Claude Code writes as it works and pulls out the latest tool calls and messages, so the agent bubbles stay current even between hook events.
docs/brainstorms/ai-onboarding-flow-requ: This is the original requirements document for making Constellation installable by a complete stranger in a single paste — the problem, the constraints, and what needs to exist.
docs/brainstorms/visualizer-text-and-pin: This is the original requirements document for fixing the three text-display problems and adding click-to-pin — the pain points and exactly what needs to change.
docs/brainstorms/zoom-and-lod-requiremen: This is the original requirements document for adding scroll-zoom, drag-pan, and the detail slider — explaining why the old static map was too coarse for large repos.
docs/ideation/2026-04-30-elegance-review: This is a brainstorm for a new code-review persona focused on elegance and readability, exploring what gap it would fill compared to the reviewers that already exist.
docs/plans/2026-04-30-001-feat-visualize: This is the step-by-step implementation plan for fixing text clipping in tiles and adding click-to-pin.
docs/plans/2026-04-30-002-feat-ai-onboar: This is the step-by-step implementation plan for making Constellation installable in a single copy-pasteable command.
docs/plans/2026-05-01-001-feat-richer-de: This is the plan for teaching the description extractor to find comments in more file types and to look past framework directives like 'use client' that appear before the actual description.
docs/plans/2026-05-01-001-feat-zoom-and-: This is the step-by-step implementation plan for adding scroll-zoom, drag-pan, and the detail slider to the map.
docs/solutions/ui-bugs/description-trunc: This records how a tile-description display bug was traced to two simultaneous mistakes — the scanner was chopping descriptions before they reached the tiles, and the tile's height math didn't account for its own borders.
docs/solutions/ui-bugs/lod-gate-only-cul: This records how the detail slider was fixed — it was hiding only a directory's children but leaving the directory's own label tile visible at any size, making the slider feel broken for small individual files.
hooks/useAgentLifecycle.ts: This tracks each agent's arrival and departure, giving dots a smooth fade-in when they appear and a fade-out when they leave instead of popping in and out abruptly.
hooks/useAgentPolling.ts: This asks the server for the current agent list on a regular interval — an older approach kept around as a fallback while the live-stream version is in use.
hooks/useAgentPositions.ts: This figures out where on your screen each agent dot should sit by reading the actual position of the file tile it's anchored to, updating whenever you zoom, pan, or resize the window.
hooks/useAgentStream.ts: This opens a live connection to the server and keeps the agent list updated in under a second, falling back to periodic polling if the connection drops.
hooks/useIdleClock.ts: This ticks a clock a few times per second so the map can tell the difference between an agent that is actively working and one that has been sitting still long enough to be considered idle.
install.sh: This is the one-shot global installer — it offers to install any missing prerequisites (Homebrew, git, jq, Node), clones the project, builds the background process and the visualizer website, puts the 'constellation' command on your PATH, and sets both up to start automatically at login on Mac.
lib/classify.ts: This looks at a thing a file shares with the rest of the app and decides what kind of thing it is — a visual element, a page route, a hook, a type — based on where the file lives and how the thing is named.
lib/config.ts: This reads Constellation's settings — the ports, the watched tools, the staleness timeout — from a single file in your home folder, seeding it from bundled defaults the very first time.
lib/constants.ts: This is the single list of sizes, timing values, and color settings that the map and the agent display draw from — change a number here and it takes effect everywhere at once.
lib/daemon-client.ts: This is a small set of helpers the home page uses to ask the background process which repos it knows about and what agents are running, silently returning empty lists if the process is down.
lib/scan.ts: This reads every file in your project, extracts descriptions and exported names, maps out which files talk to which, and hands the whole picture to the map.
lib/scan/description-sidecar.ts: This loads the hand-written descriptions from a '.constellation/descriptions.json' (or YAML) file and lets them override anything the automatic extractor found.
lib/scan/descriptions.ts: This opens each file and looks for a leading comment block — JSDoc for code files, hash blocks for shell and YAML, docstrings for Python, and so on — and returns the text as the tile's description.
lib/scan/discover.ts: This walks the project folder, skips build output and generated files, measures the size of everything it finds, and collapses directories that are too huge to load into a single placeholder tile.
lib/scan/imports.ts: This maps out which files pull from which other files inside the project, so hovering a tile can highlight its dependencies and dependents on the map.
lib/scan/symbols.ts: This reads each TypeScript file and lists what it shares with the rest of the project — the things you'd see in the hover card's 'Exports' section.
lib/scan/synthetic.ts: This manufactures a fake 5,000-file project out of thin air for the zoom performance test page — same shape as a real repo but no disk reading required.
lib/scan/tree.ts: This takes all the per-file information gathered by the other scan phases and assembles it into the nested folder-and-file tree the map renders.
lib/roadmap.ts: This reads the project's roadmap file from the repo it's looking at and checks that it matches the agreed shape — handing the visualizer a clean tracker to display, or nothing at all if the file is missing or broken.
lib/treemap.ts: This is the math that decides how big each rectangle on the map should be and where it sits, slicing the available space to keep tiles roughly square rather than long and thin.
lib/types.ts: This is the shared set of shapes the rest of the app passes around — what a file looks like, what kinds of things a file can export, and what a running agent looks like.
lib/user-dirs.ts: This figures out where Constellation keeps all its files on your machine — the settings, the saved agent state, the registered repos list, and the process ID — so every part of the app agrees on the same location.
LICENSE: This is the legal permission slip that says anyone can use, copy, or build on this project as long as they keep the copyright notice.
next.config.ts: Wiring — connects other pieces together but doesn't really do anything on its own.
package.json: This is the project's name tag and shopping list — it says what this project is called, what other projects it relies on, and the commands you can run.
postcss.config.mjs: Wiring — connects other pieces together but doesn't really do anything on its own.
README.md: This is the project's front door — it explains what Constellation does, how to install it, and how to start using it.
roadmap.json: This is the project tracker — what you're working on right now, what you want to ship in the next few days, weeks, and months, plus what just shipped, what's broken, what you're unsure about, and what's parked. Edit it as a side effect of doing work.
roadmap.schema.json: This is the rulebook for the project tracker — it spells out exactly which sections must exist in roadmap.json and what each item is allowed to contain, so the file can't quietly drift when the AI updates it.
scripts/dev.mjs: This is the development supervisor — when you run 'npm run dev', it starts both the background process and the web visualizer side by side, and shuts them both down together on Ctrl-C.
scripts/install-settings.mjs: This is the settings-merge step of the installer — it shows you exactly what will change in your Claude Code settings, including the hook scripts that will run, then writes the file only after you confirm.
scripts/web-server.mjs: This is the launcher macOS uses to keep the visualizer website running in the background — it reads the chosen port from settings and starts the web server, restarting automatically if it ever crashes.
service/com.constellation.daemon.plist.t: This is the template that gets filled in and registered with macOS to keep the background process running at login and restart it automatically if it ever crashes.
service/com.constellation.web.plist.temp: This is the template that gets filled in and registered with macOS to keep the visualizer website running at login and restart it automatically if it ever crashes.
tsconfig.daemon.json: This is the build settings for compiling just the background process to plain runnable files so macOS's launch system can start it directly.
tsconfig.json: This is the language settings for the web app half of the project — it tells the tools how to understand the code and where to find shared pieces.
